text:
Mikael Granlund is 34, on his sixth NHL team, and having one of the most productive stretches of his career. He has points in seven straight games (4 goals, 10 assists), 22 points in 18 games overall, and Anaheim has pushed his minutes past 21 a night over his last ten. He was a big part of the winning streak Nashville snapped on Wednesday.

Our numbers aren't buying all of it. His scoring rate of 3.56 points per 60 is well above the 2.5 our talent range expects, and the Ducks have scored 9.1 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. His own shooting, 18% against a range near 15%, is also running warm.

The five-on-five picture is the concern. Anaheim gets under 40% of the expected goals with him out there, almost seven points worse than when he sits. Last season told a different story: Evolving-Hockey had him in the 90th percentile among forwards for creating expected goals. He still moves the puck cleanly out of his own end. Watch whether his line starts generating more than it gives up, because the bounces paying for the gap won't last.
headline: Granlund's points are outrunning his line
